newsitem.title: FINLAND: EU summit main focus for Finnish markets next week.
newsitem.headline: EU summit main focus for Finnish markets next week.

text.p: Finnish markets will focus on the December 12-14 EU meetings in Dublin, and primarily on the fate of the EMU stability pact.
U.S. November PPI and CPI figures, due December 11 and 12, will also be watched closely by the markets, analysts said.

The fate of the stability pact will be at stake in Dublin, said Carlo Erakalio, chief economist at Handelsbanken Markets. The budget stability pact is among the most important issues for the future of EMU.
Stock market operators will also monitor the outcome of the Dublin summit, analysts said.
STABILITY PACT SETBACK MAY HURT STOCKS
"If there appears any setbacks at the meeting, it can cause disturbances," said Mika Koskinen, analyst at Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken in Helsinki.
He noted that the Finnish share market is strongly driven by low interest rates, which could be hit if the meeting does not proceed as expected.

Jukka Lepomaki, chief analyst at Merita Bank, said that bonds in peripheral countries like Finland may suffer if EU leaders fail to strike a deal on the budget stability pact, while German bunds would gain.
The Finnish currency is not expected to weaken as "the markka seems to have fundamentals of its own", Lepomaki said.
He added that an order for two big cruise vessels won by Masa Yards, part of Norwegian Kvaerner A/S, worth around one billion dollars, was expected to continue to support the markka in the future.
U.S. INDICATORS MAY AFFECT STOCKS

Finnish shares are sensitive to price changes in U.S. stocks. If U.S. November PPI and CPI differ markedly from forecasts resulting in big moves in U.S. shares, the Helsinki bourse is expected to follow.
The inflation figures are also expected to give clues to future U.S. monetary policy.
"Only if very bearish figures are published could speculation emerge about a rate hike (in the U.S.)," Lepomaki said.

U.S. November PPI will be published on Wednesday at 1530/1330 GMT. In October, producer prices rose 0.4 percent month-on-month. U.S. CPI will be released on Thursday at 1530/1330 GMT. In October, the CPI rise was 0.3 percent.
T-BILLS INTERESTING
On Tuesday, the Finnish State Treasury Office (STO) will hold its regular weekly T-bill auction.
STO will announce on Thursday at 1600/1400 GMT the maturities to be auctioned.
"The short end (of the yield curve) is likely to be of interest as bonds have lately been bought in large amounts," Lepomaki said. The auction results will be annouced after 1330/1130 GMT. @
FINNISH INDICATORS NOT "HOT"
On Thursday, Statistics Finland (SF) will release the November consumer barometer at 0700/0500 GMT. It will be closely studied but is not expected to move the market, analysts said.
In October, the consumer confidence gauge fell to 12.0 from 14.2 in September -- the first decline since April.

November construction costs will be published at 0700/0500 GMT on Friday. In October, construction costs fell by 0.8 percent year-on-year. Analysts said the figures will be largely ignored even if they show strong growth as the costs are low at the moment. -- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 245
